questions.q: What is the standard shape of a case lifecycle, per this lesson?
options: New, then In Progress while a rep works it, possibly Escalated, then Closed
Closed, then New, then In Progress
Escalated is always the first stage
There is no standard pattern at all across orgs
questions.explain: That open, being worked, possibly escalated, closed pattern is standard across Service Cloud implementations.

questions.q: What varies from org to org in the case lifecycle, per this lesson?
options: The exact wording of the picklist values for each stage
Whether cases have a Status field at all
Whether a case can ever be closed
Whether the Case object exists in Service Cloud
questions.explain: The pattern is standard, but the exact picklist wording (e.g. 'Working' vs. 'In Progress') is configured per org.

questions.q: What do Case Assignment Rules do, per this lesson?
options: Automatically route a new Case to the right owner based on criteria like Origin or Priority
Automatically close cases after 24 hours
Delete cases that have been open too long
Change a Contact's Account
questions.explain: Assignment Rules are admin-configured logic that routes a new case to a rep or queue instead of leaving it unassigned.

questions.q: Why do Case Assignment Rules matter directly to an analyst, per this lesson?
options: 'Time to first response' is measured from case creation, so a delay in assignment is dead time baked into that metric
They have no effect on any metric an analyst would report
They determine the Case Number
They set the customer's billing address
questions.explain: A case sitting unassigned before a rule routes it adds directly to the time-to-first-response metric.

questions.q: What do Escalation Rules do, and why should an analyst track escalations separately?
options: They automatically escalate cases open too long for their priority; a rising escalation count is an early sign of a support team falling behind
They automatically escalate every case regardless of priority
They are identical to Assignment Rules and serve no separate purpose
They only apply to closed cases
questions.explain: Escalation Rules watch for cases meeting certain lagging conditions, and a rising escalation count can signal trouble before overall volume does.
